issues.legal_issue: A widow’s limited interest in property created by an instrument is not enlarged into full ownership where she had no pre-existing right in the property and the instrument prescribes a restricted estate.
material_facts: The widow’s husband died in 1925, and under the Hindu law then applicable she acquired no share or interest in the house left by him.
A registered award later entitled her to receive the house’s rent in lieu of maintenance for her lifetime and provided that her sons would own the house after her death.
The widow claimed the house in proceedings concerning its attachment and argued that her limited interest had become full ownership.
Her interest ended during the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The award created a restricted estate within the scope of Section 14(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956; Section 14(1) did not enlarge the widow’s interest, which ended on her death. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) enlarges a woman’s interest where she possesses property in recognition of a pre-existing right, but Section 14(2) applies where a gift, will, instrument, decree, order, or award itself prescribes a restricted estate. Badri Prasad v. Smt. Kanan Devi was distinguished because the widow there acquired a share under the Hindu Women’s Right to Property Act, 1937, and therefore had a pre-existing right; the widow here had none, and the award created her restricted estate.

rule.if: succession_appeal and instrument_grants_only_lifetime_income and no_preexisting_property_right and instrument_names_others_as_owners_after_life

predicates.succession_appeal: An appeal concerns whether a widow’s limited interest in property was enlarged into full ownership under succession law.
predicates.instrument_grants_only_lifetime_income: An instrument gives a widow income from property only for her lifetime.
predicates.no_preexisting_property_right: The widow had no right or interest in the property before the instrument created her interest.
predicates.instrument_names_others_as_owners_after_: The instrument provides that other people will own the property after the widow’s lifetime interest ends.
predicates.widow_limited_interest_ends_at_death: The widow’s limited interest in the property ends when she dies.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns enlargement of a widow’s property interest, and an instrument gives her only lifetime income despite her having no prior property right while naming others as owners afterward, her limited interest ends at her death.
